intent.raw_query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June 2026 from Chicago

experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic history.

experiences.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Private Art Experience

experiences.name: Testaccio Market Culinary Exploration
experiences.description: Dive into Rome's authentic food culture at this beloved local market. Taste offal-based Roman street food, fresh pasta, seasonal produce, and artisan gelato. Chat with vendors and join a hands-on pasta-making class at a nearby cooking school.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use this time to rest on board or prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome (Flight LH lands at 13:00). Take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini (€14, ~32 min) — the most budget-friendly fast option. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a relaxed orientation walk around your neighborhood to get your bearings, find a local supermarket, and soak in the Roman atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the nearby Piazza Navona (free entry) to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers and enjoy the lively street art scene. Watch local artists at work — a perfect low-cost introduction to Rome's art culture.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick coffee and cornetto (€2–3) at a bar near the airport or Termini station.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap supplì (fried rice ball) or a slice of pizza al taglio near Roma Termini (€3–5) after arrival.
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Lucia or a similar no-frills neighborhood trattoria near Piazza Navona — try cacio e pepe or carbonara. Budget around €12–16 per person including house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Buy a 48-hour or 72-hour public transport pass (€7/€12) at Termini to save money on buses and metro throughout the trip. Keep your hotel receipt handy for the city tourist tax (usually €3–7/night, paid at check-in).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel — book tickets online in advance to skip the line (€20 general admission). Arrive early (opening time ~09:00) to beat the crowds. Marvel at Michelangelo's ceiling and the Gallery of Maps. St. Peter's Basilica entry is FREE — don't miss it. Climb to the dome for panoramic views (€8 with elevator, €6 on foot).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cross the Tiber and walk to Castel Sant'Angelo (exterior free to admire, interior €15 but optional on a budget). Continue along the scenic riverside promenade. Head to the Trastevere neighborhood — one of Rome's most charming and artsy districts — for a leisurely afternoon wander through cobblestone streets, colorful murals, and local boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the bohemian evening atmosphere of Trastevere. Browse local street art and admire the Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free, beautifully lit at night).

meals.breakfast: Espresso and cornetto at a local bar near your hotel (€2–3). Avoid sitting down — standing at the bar is cheaper and more authentic.
meals.lunch: Mercato di Porta Portese area or a Trastevere forno (bakery) — pick up fresh bread, local cheese, and cured meats for a picnic by the Tiber (€5–8).
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — a beloved budget-friendly Roman trattoria. Try rigatoni alla gricia or abbacchio. Budget €14–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Vatican can be overwhelming — wear comfortable shoes and bring a water bottle (there are free drinking fountains called 'nasoni' throughout Rome). Shoulders and knees must be covered to enter St. Peter's Basilica — bring a scarf.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill (combined ticket with the Colosseum, €18 — book online to skip queues). Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire and imagine life 2,000 years ago. The Palatine Hill offers stunning panoramic views over the Forum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Colosseum (included in your combined ticket). Then head to the nearby Circus Maximus (free) and take a leisurely walk through the Aventine Hill. Don't miss the famous Knights of Malta keyhole (Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta) — a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome, completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Testaccio neighborhood, Rome's traditional working-class food district. Browse the Testaccio Market area (closes by afternoon but the neighborhood stays lively) and enjoy the local vibe.

meals.breakfast: Bar near your hotel — cappuccino and pastry (€2.50–4).
meals.lunch: Grab street food near the Colosseum — avoid tourist traps and walk one block back to find pizza al taglio or a panino shop (€4–7).
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — famous for authentic Roman cuisine at honest prices. Try the coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew). Budget €15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The combined Forum/Palatine/Colosseum ticket is valid for 24 hours across all three sites — plan accordingly. Testaccio is also home to the city's best gelato spots — try Fatamorgana for artisan flavors (€2.50–3.50 per scoop).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery — one of Rome's finest art collections featuring Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings. IMPORTANT: reservations are mandatory and entry is strictly timed (€15 + €2 booking fee). Book well in advance. Spend the morning surrounded by world-class baroque art in an intimate setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy a free stroll through the vast Villa Borghese park — Rome's Central Park. Rent a rowboat on the lake (€3–5), relax on the grass, or explore the park's free viewpoints overlooking the city. Walk down to the Spanish Steps (Piazza di Spagna) — free to visit, though swimming in the Trevi Fountain area is prohibited.
day_by_day.evening: Toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain (free, just the coin!) and explore the surrounding streets. Head to the Campo de' Fiori for the evening market atmosphere and aperitivo hour.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh pastry and coffee at a local bar (€2–3).
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese park — buy supplies from a nearby alimentari (deli): bread, prosciutto, olives, and fruit (€6–9). Eat surrounded by greenery and art.
meals.dinner: Campo de' Fiori area — try Forno Campo de' Fiori for incredible pizza bianca (€3–5) as a snack, then find a side-street trattoria for a full dinner (€12–16 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Borghese Gallery only admits 360 visitors at a time in 2-hour slots — this intimate experience is well worth the advance planning. The Spanish Steps area can be crowded; visit in the early evening for a better experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Capitoline Museums (€15) — the world's oldest public museums, housing iconic works like the Capitoline Wolf, Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, and stunning views over the Roman Forum from the terrace. A must for art lovers. Spend the morning exploring ancient Roman and Renaissance art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Pantheon (€5 entry — recently began charging admission). Marvel at the 2,000-year-old unreinforced concrete dome — still the largest in the world. Then explore the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood nearby — one of Rome's oldest and most historically rich areas with free outdoor monuments and beautiful architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Pigneto neighborhood — Rome's up-and-coming creative district full of street art, independent galleries, and a young local crowd. A great alternative to tourist-heavy areas.

meals.breakfast: Try a local bar in the Jewish Ghetto area — try a Jewish-Roman pastry like carciofi alla giudia (fried artichoke) if available as a morning snack (€3–5).
meals.lunch: Eat at a Jewish-Roman restaurant in the Ghetto — try supplì and carciofi alla giudia at Nonna Betta or a similar spot (€10–14 per person).
meals.dinner: Pigneto neighborhood — try Primo al Pigneto or a local osteria for creative Roman cuisine at non-tourist prices (€14–18 per person). Enjoy an aperitivo at one of the neighborhood bars (€5–7 with snacks).

day_by_day.notes: The Capitoline Museums offer free admission on the first Sunday of each month — if your dates align, take advantage! The Pantheon is best visited mid-morning on a weekday to avoid peak crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free morning to explore the Appian Way (Via Appia Antica) — one of the world's oldest roads, lined with ancient tombs, ruins, and catacombs. Rent a bike near the park entrance (€3–5/hour) and cycle through history. Visit the Catacombs of San Callisto (€10) — an extraordinary underground Christian burial site with fascinating early Christian art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city center and visit the lesser-known but stunning Basilica di San Clemente (€10) — three layers of history stacked underground: a medieval church, a 4th-century basilica, and an ancient Roman building with a Mithraic temple. A hidden gem beloved by art and history enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your second-to-last evening revisiting your favorite neighborhood or exploring the Monti district — Rome's trendy bohemian quarter with independent vintage shops, art galleries, and cozy wine bars (enoteca).

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at your hotel or a nearby bar (€2–4).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the Appian Way — grab supplies from a local market: focaccia, cheese, fruit, and water (€6–8). Eat among ancient ruins.
meals.dinner: Monti neighborhood — try Alle Carrette for excellent thin-crust pizza (€7–12 per person) or explore the local enoteca scene with wine and charcuterie boards (€10–15 per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Appian Way is best visited on weekdays — on Sundays it's closed to cars and very popular with locals for cycling and walking. Wear sunscreen and bring water as the road is exposed. San Clemente is an underrated gem — rarely crowded and deeply rewarding for art lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — visit any missed sites or return to your favorite spots. Consider the free Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore (one of Rome's four major basilicas) or the beautiful Palazzo Doria Pamphilj gallery (€15) with works by Velázquez, Caravaggio, and Raphael. Alternatively, spend a leisurely morning shopping for food souvenirs at a local market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping — avoid tourist shops near major sights and instead visit Campo de' Fiori market (open until ~14:00) or local delis for authentic Italian products: dried pasta, olive oil, bottled sauces, and local wines at real prices. Pack your bags and do a final neighborhood walk.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at your favorite restaurant from the week, or splurge slightly on a special Roman meal to end the trip on a high note. Raise a glass of local Frascati wine to a wonderful week in Rome.

meals.breakfast: A proper Roman sit-down breakfast at a historic café — try Sant'Eustachio il Caffè near the Pantheon for arguably Rome's best espresso (€2–4 standing at the bar).
meals.lunch: Light lunch — supplì, pizza al taglio, or a sandwich from a local forno (€4–7). Keep it simple to save room for dinner.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly elevated farewell dinner — try Osteria dell'Ingegno near the Pantheon or a local favorite discovered during your week. Budget €18–25 per person for a memorable final meal with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Check your departure details carefully. If flying from Fiumicino, allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the train journey and airport check-in. The Leonardo Express runs every 30 minutes from Roma Termini. Keep some euros aside for the train fare back to the airport (€14). Don't forget to use up any remaining public transport passes!

trip_options.title: Classic Rome Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Rome — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely orientation stroll around your hotel's neighborhood. Head to the nearby waterfront promenade or a local piazza to get your bearings, pick up a city map, and soak in the Roman atmosphere. Visit a nearby gelateria for your first authentic Italian gelato.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle introduction to Roman dining culture. Head to a mid-range trattoria within walking distance of the hotel for a classic Roman dinner — try cacio e pepe or carbonara to kick off the trip on a high note.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick espresso and cornetto at the airport or on arrival — no formal breakfast scheduled today.
meals.lunch: Light bite near the hotel after check-in: a neighborhood bar or café serving tramezzini (Italian sandwiches) or a simple pizza al taglio (pizza by the slice).
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Enzo al 29 (or similar local trattoria near your hotel) — mid-range Roman classics, around €25–35 per person including wine.

day_by_day.notes: Since the flight lands at 13:00, allow roughly 1–1.5 hours for baggage claim and transfer to the hotel. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel. Confirm hotel check-in time in advance in case early check-in is needed.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Book the first entry slot (08:00–09:00) to beat the crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring one of the world's greatest art collections: the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Pre-book skip-the-line tickets online (€20–27 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross the Tiber to explore Castel Sant'Angelo and stroll along the Lungotevere riverside. Then head into the charming Prati neighborhood for a mid-afternoon coffee break and window shopping at local boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour — Join an evening guided tour through Rome's most charming medieval neighborhood. Sample supplì (fried rice balls), artisanal cheeses, and local wines while wandering cobblestone lanes. Tours typically run 18:30–21:00 (approx. €65–80 per person).

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast at the hotel or a nearby bar: espresso, cappuccino, and a fresh cornetto — €3–5 per person.
meals.lunch: Quick and authentic lunch in the Borgo neighborhood near the Vatican: a classic Roman pizzeria or a sandwich from a local alimentari (deli). Budget €12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour tastings. If still hungry afterward, grab a final glass of wine and a bruschetta at a Trastevere wine bar like Enoteca Ferrara.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums are extremely popular — pre-booking tickets weeks in advance is strongly recommended. Dress code applies: cover shoulders and knees for the Sistine Chapel. Comfortable walking shoes are essential today.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Private Art Experience — Start the day with a pre-booked private or small-group visit to the Borghese Gallery (entry is strictly timed, 2-hour slots starting at 09:00). Discover Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in one of Rome's most intimate and beautiful museums. Tickets must be reserved in advance (€13 entry + booking fee; private experience €80–120 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, enjoy a relaxing walk through the Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's green lung. Rent a rowboat on the small lake or simply picnic under the pines. Then descend into the Tridente neighborhood to explore the Spanish Steps, Piazza del Popolo, and the Via Condotti luxury shopping street (window shopping is free!).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Campo de' Fiori market square in the evening (the market itself is morning-only, but the piazza buzzes at night). Enjoy aperitivo hour with a Aperol Spritz or Negroni at a sidewalk bar, then dine at a nearby osteria.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick café stop near the Borghese Gallery: cappuccino and pastry, €4–6.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up fresh bread, cheese, prosciutto, olives, and fruit from a nearby deli or supermarket. Budget €10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Osteria del Pegno or similar mid-range osteria near Campo de' Fiori — Roman classics like coda alla vaccinara (oxtail stew) or saltimbocca alla romana. Budget €30–40 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery only admits 360 visitors every 2 hours — booking is absolutely mandatory, often weeks ahead. The gallery does not allow re-entry once you leave, so plan your visit carefully within the 2-hour window.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market Culinary Exploration — Arrive early (09:00–10:00) at Rome's beloved local food market in the Testaccio neighborhood. Taste offal-based Roman street food, fresh produce, artisan cheeses, and local specialties. Chat with vendors and learn about Roman food culture. This is a self-guided or guided experience (guided tours approx. €45–60 per person; self-guided is free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Testaccio neighborhood further — visit the Non-Catholic Cemetery (where Keats and Shelley are buried, a peaceful and beautiful spot), and see the Pyramid of Cestius. Then head to the Circus Maximus and the Aventine Hill for the famous Knights of Malta keyhole view of St. Peter's Basilica and the serene Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a mid-evening rest, then head out for a classic Roman aperitivo followed by dinner at a neighborhood restaurant near your hotel's beachfront area, trying local seafood dishes given the coastal setting.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Testaccio Market itself — a supplì (fried rice ball), a fresh pastry, and an espresso from the market vendors. Budget €5–8.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Testaccio at Flavio al Velavevodetto or similar — a beloved local trattoria known for authentic Roman cuisine. Try rigatoni alla pajata or carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style artichokes). Budget €20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner near the hotel's beachfront area — grilled branzino (sea bass), spaghetti alle vongole (clams), or fritto misto. Budget €28–40 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Testaccio Market is open Monday–Saturday, typically 07:00–14:00. Arrive before 11:00 for the best selection and atmosphere. The Testaccio neighborhood is considered the birthplace of Roman cuisine — a must for food lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Morning Visit — Head to the ancient heart of Rome early (tickets open at 09:00) to explore the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill before the midday heat. Walk among millennia-old temples, triumphal arches, and imperial palaces. Combined ticket with the Colosseum (€16–18 per person) — consider adding a Colosseum visit if energy allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the ancient sites, take a short walk to the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood — one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric quarters. Browse the historic streets, visit the Great Synagogue of Rome (Museo Ebraico, €11 entry), and explore the area around Largo di Torre Argentina (the cat sanctuary and ancient temple ruins — free to view from above).
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour (optional upgrade) — If you prefer the golden-hour atmosphere over the morning visit, swap the morning and evening slots. Otherwise, enjoy a relaxed evening near the Pantheon area: toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain at dusk (beautiful and less crowded than midday), then dine nearby.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the Colosseo metro stop — cornetto and cappuccino, €4–6.
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Jewish Ghetto — try the famous carciofi alla giudia (crispy fried artichokes) and Jewish-Roman specialties at Nonna Betta or Ba'Ghetto. Budget €22–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner near the Pantheon — Ristorante La Campana (one of Rome's oldest restaurants) or a nearby enoteca. Try abbacchio alla romana (Roman-style lamb) or a classic pasta dish. Budget €30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Roman Forum and Palatine Hill are very exposed to the sun — bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water, especially in June when temperatures can reach 30–35°C. The combined Colosseum/Forum/Palatine ticket is valid for 2 consecutive days.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicated Art Morning — Visit the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna (GNAM) near Villa Borghese for a deep dive into 19th and 20th-century Italian art, or alternatively explore the Palazzo Altemps (part of the National Roman Museum) for its outstanding classical sculpture collection. A quieter, more contemplative museum experience away from the tourist rush. Entry €10–12 per person.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Piazza Navona area — admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, browse the artist stalls, and duck into the church of Sant'Agnese in Agone (free). Then wander through the antique and artisan shops of the surrounding streets. Visit the nearby Palazzo Doria Pamphilj if time allows (private palace with a remarkable art collection, €14 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Final big-night dinner experience — splurge slightly on a well-regarded mid-to-upper-range Roman restaurant for a memorable meal. Consider a restaurant offering a tasting menu of Roman cuisine classics with local wine pairings.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a neighborhood café near the hotel — fresh-squeezed orange juice, cappuccino, and a brioche. €5–8.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a wine bar (enoteca) near Piazza Navona — a selection of cured meats, cheeses, bruschetta, and a glass of local Frascati white wine. Budget €18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Il Sorpasso or Roscioli (book ahead) — celebrated mid-range Roman restaurants with outstanding wine lists and seasonal menus. Budget €40–55 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday in Rome can be busy, especially around Piazza Navona and the historic center. Book dinner reservations well in advance. The Palazzo Doria Pamphilj is a hidden gem — often overlooked by tourists but holds works by Velázquez, Titian, and Caravaggio.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in Rome — On Sunday mornings, the Porta Portese flea market (07:00–14:00) is a Rome institution — browse hundreds of stalls for vintage clothing, antiques, books, and local curiosities in the Trastevere area. A wonderful, authentic Roman experience. Alternatively, attend Sunday Mass at St. Peter's Basilica (free, no ticket needed for the Basilica itself) for a spiritual and architectural farewell.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute sightseeing and souvenir shopping. Revisit a favorite neighborhood or landmark at a slower pace. Stop by a local pasticceria to pick up biscotti, torrone, or other edible souvenirs to bring home. Pack bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner near the hotel — keep it relaxed and local. Choose a neighborhood restaurant you noticed during the week, or return to a favorite spot from earlier in the trip. Toast to a wonderful Roman holiday.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick espresso and pastry at a bar near Porta Portese before the market, or enjoy a final hotel breakfast. €3–6.
meals.lunch: Sunday lunch at a classic Roman trattoria in Trastevere — many Romans do a long, leisurely Sunday lunch. Try cacio e pepe, supplì, and tiramisu for dessert. Budget €25–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a beloved neighborhood restaurant near the hotel — keep it simple and meaningful. A wood-fired pizza, a carafe of house wine, and a final scoop of gelato for dessert. Budget €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check your return flight details and plan airport transfer time accordingly. Porta Portese flea market runs Sunday mornings only — don't miss it if you enjoy markets. Leave time to pick up any last-minute food souvenirs: Roman pecorino cheese, dried pasta, or a bottle of local Lazio wine make excellent gifts.

day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on a rooftop bar with views toward Castel Sant'Angelo — try the Settimio all'Arancio terrace or the hotel Raphael rooftop. Follow with dinner at a refined trattoria in Prati, focusing on classic Roman pasta dishes executed with premium ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full Italian breakfast at the resort — cornetti, granita, fresh-pressed orange juice, cappuccino, and seasonal fruit platters
meals.lunch: Ristorante Il Sorpasso (Prati) — elevated Roman cuisine with an exceptional natural wine list; try the supplì al telefono and house-made tonnarelli cacio e pepe
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo or La Pergola (Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant, book weeks in advance) — panoramic views and extraordinary tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Vatican skip-the-line private tour well in advance — ideally 4–6 weeks ahead. Wear comfortable shoes; expect 3–4 hours of walking. Dress code for St. Peter's: covered shoulders and knees required.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Private Art Experience — Reserve the first time slot (09:00) for maximum intimacy. A private guide walks you through Bernini's extraordinary sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic canvases. Entry is strictly timed and limited to 360 visitors per session — the private experience elevates this significantly. Afterward, stroll through the manicured Villa Borghese gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Testaccio Market Culinary Exploration — Transfer to Rome's most authentic food market. A local chef-guide leads you through stalls of seasonal produce, aged cheeses, cured meats, and offal-based Roman street food. Sample supplì, porchetta sandwiches, fried artichokes (carciofi alla giudia), and finish with a scoop of artisan gelato. This is Rome's true food soul.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour in Testaccio followed by dinner at one of the neighborhood's beloved trattorias. Testaccio is Rome's culinary heartland — unpretentious but exceptional. Finish with a digestivo passeggiata along the Tiber riverbanks.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — add a fresh-made frittata station and smoked salmon to the standard spread; request in advance
meals.lunch: Included in the Testaccio Market tour — grazing through market stalls with your guide; supplemented with a sit-down primo at a market-adjacent café
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) — legendary Roman trattoria carved into Monte dei Cocci (ancient amphora shards); order the rigatoni con pajata and coda alla vaccinara

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery is one of Rome's most sought-after experiences — book private access 6–8 weeks in advance. The gallery limits total visitors strictly. Testaccio Market is liveliest before noon; the afternoon tour works well as a late-morning-into-afternoon experience.

day_by_day.morning: Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour — Begin at 09:30 in Rome's most enchanting medieval neighborhood. Wander cobblestone alleys with a sommelier-guide, sampling supplì, artisan cheeses, house-cured salumi, wood-fired pizza al taglio, and local Frascati white wine. Visit a century-old forno (bakery) and a tiny family-run olive oil producer. The tour culminates at a scenic piazza with a final wine tasting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Free afternoon for personal exploration in Trastevere. Browse the antique markets and independent art galleries along Via della Lungaretta. Visit the stunning Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere — one of Rome's oldest churches with extraordinary golden mosaics. Enjoy a slow afternoon espresso at Bar San Calisto, a Trastevere institution.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a scenic terrace overlooking the Janiculum Hill, then a refined dinner back in Trastevere — the neighborhood transforms beautifully at night with candlelit alleyways and ambient music.

meals.breakfast: Light resort breakfast before the food tour — keep it minimal as the tour includes substantial tastings
meals.lunch: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Walking Tour — multiple tastings across 5–6 stops throughout the neighborhood
meals.dinner: Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio or Tonnarello — Trastevere's classic upscale trattoria with outdoor terrace seating; order the cacio e pepe and artichoke alla romana

day_by_day.notes: Wear very comfortable walking shoes — Trastevere's cobblestones are uneven. The food tour is best enjoyed with an appetite; skip a heavy resort breakfast. The neighborhood is magical at golden hour — leave time to simply wander without agenda.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour — Book the morning private guided session (09:00–12:00) to beat the heat and crowds. Walk through the birthplace of Rome: the Palatine Hill where emperors built their palaces, overlooking the Roman Forum's temples, basilicas, and the Sacred Way. A knowledgeable archaeologist-guide brings 2,000 years of history to vivid life. Includes the Colosseum exterior viewing.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the ancient ruins, refresh at a nearby luxury café in the Celio neighborhood. Then visit the Capitoline Museums — the world's oldest public museums — housing the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and extraordinary ancient Roman sculpture collections. End with a coffee at the museum's rooftop café with views of the Forum below.
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour (alternative: if the morning session was taken, book the sunset version at 18:30 instead for dramatic golden-hour lighting over the ruins). Dinner at a Michelin-recognized restaurant in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — request a packed espresso and cornetto to take on the go if departing early
meals.lunch: Ristorante Aroma (rooftop with Colosseum views, Michelin-starred) — the ultimate Roman lunch setting; book well in advance; try the Roman-style sea bass and house-made pasta
meals.dinner: Pipero Roma — one of Rome's most celebrated contemporary fine dining restaurants; innovative tasting menu with Roman flavor anchors; exceptional sommelier service

day_by_day.notes: The Colosseum, Forum, and Palatine Hill are covered under a combined ticket. Private guided access is essential for depth of experience. June heat can be intense by midday — bring a hat, sunscreen, and water. The Aroma restaurant reservation at lunch with Colosseum views is one of Rome's most iconic dining moments.

day_by_day.morning: Private atelier art tour of Rome's lesser-known masterpieces — arranged through the hotel concierge. Visit the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj (private noble family still in residence), housing Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and Caravaggio's Rest on the Flight into Egypt. Then the Galleria Corsini for Raphael and Rubens. Finish at the Palazzo Barberini for more Caravaggio and Pietro da Cortona's breathtaking ceiling fresco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping along Via Condotti and Piazza di Spagna — Rome's golden mile of haute couture. Browse Bulgari, Valentino, Fendi's flagship, and artisan leather goods at Ibiz. Stop for a legendary Caffè Greco espresso (operating since 1760, frequented by Keats, Goethe, and Byron). Afternoon gelato at Giolitti or Della Palma.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the Hotel de Russie's Stravinskij Bar — one of Rome's most glamorous hotel bars, beloved by celebrities and dignitaries. Followed by a grand final dinner at a celebrated restaurant of your choosing — La Pergola if not visited on Day 2, or return to a favorite discovery from the week.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely resort breakfast — full spread with made-to-order eggs, pastries, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Dal Bolognese (Piazza del Popolo) — Rome's most glamorous classic trattoria, beloved by the fashion and film world; tagliatelle al ragù and vitello tonnato are essential orders
meals.dinner: La Pergola (Rome Cavalieri Hotel) — Chef Heinz Beck's three-Michelin-star masterpiece; 8-course tasting menu with wine pairing; one of Italy's finest dining experiences; formal dress required

day_by_day.notes: Via Condotti boutiques close for riposo 13:00–15:30 — plan shopping either before 13:00 or after 15:30. La Pergola requires formal attire (jacket required for gentlemen) and advance booking of 4–8 weeks minimum. The Palazzo Doria Pamphilj audio guide narrated by the current Prince Doria Pamphilj himself is a charming touch.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — slow and indulgent. Sleep in, enjoy a long resort breakfast on the beachfront terrace watching the morning light over the water. Optional: a sunrise or early-morning private yoga session on the beach arranged through the resort. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last Roman experience: visit Campo de' Fiori's Sunday market for artisan food souvenirs — aged Pecorino, truffle products, local olive oils, and handmade pasta to bring home. Stroll to the nearby Piazza Navona for a final espresso and people-watching at one of Rome's most beautiful baroque squares. Farewell lunch at a beloved spot near the historic center.
day_by_day.evening: Private chauffeur transfer to Fiumicino Airport (allow 75–90 minutes depending on traffic). Check-in for departure flight. Lounge access arranged through concierge or premium credit card. Depart Rome with extraordinary memories of art, food, and la dolce vita.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — request a special spread: fresh sfogliatelle, Sicilian cannoli, Roman maritozzi con panna, seasonal fruit, and a bottle of chilled Franciacorta
meals.lunch: Osteria del Pegno or Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio — final Roman lunch; order whatever you didn't get to try during the week; finish with a classic tiramisù
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or light meal — or an early dinner in the historic center before transfer if the flight departure allows

day_by_day.notes: Purchase artisan food souvenirs before 13:00 as Sunday market stalls close early. Allow ample time for airport transfer — Rome traffic on Sunday afternoons can be unpredictable. Ask the hotel to arrange a beautiful farewell amenity or parting gift (many luxury hotels offer this). Keep one final espresso at the airport as your last taste of Rome.

query: Rome art and food trip, $2500, 7 days, June 2026 from Chicago
